Use "fleet completion [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(fleet completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	fleet completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/fleet

#### macOS:

	fleet completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/fleet

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

Usage:
  fleet completion bash

Flags:
  -h, --help              help for bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	fleet completion fish | source

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(fleet completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	fleet completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_fleet"

#### macOS:

	fleet completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_fleet

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

  fleet completion zsh [flags]

Dump the parsed configuration in yaml format.

Fleet retrieves configuration options from many locations, and it can be
useful to see the result of merging those configs.

The following precedence is used when reading configs:
1. CLI flags
2. Environment Variables
3. Config File
4. Default Values

The vuln_processing command is intended for advanced configurations that want to externally manage
vulnerability processing. By default the Fleet server command internally manages vulnerability processing via scheduled
'cron' style jobs, but setting 'vulnerabilities.disable_schedule=true' or 'FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_SCHEDULE=true'
will disable it on the server allowing the user configure their own 'cron' mechanism. Successful processing will be indicated
by an exit code of zero.

Usage:
  fleet vuln_processing [flags]

Flags:
      --dev                      Enable developer options
      --dev_expired_license      Enable expired development license
      --dev_license              Enable development license
  -h, --help                     help for vuln_processing
      --lock_duration duration   the duration (https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) the lock should be obtained, ideally this duration is less than the interval in which the job runs (defaults to 60m). If vuln processing isn't finished before this duration the command will exit with a non-zero status code. (default 1h0m0s)

vuln_processing.--redis_idle_timeout: Env: FLEET_REDIS_IDLE_TIMEOUT Redis maximum amount of time a connection may stay idle, 0 means no limit (default 4m0s)
vuln_processing.--redis_keep_alive: Env: FLEET_REDIS_KEEP_ALIVE Interval between keep alive probes (default 10s)
vuln_processing.--redis_live_query_small_target_threshol: Env: FLEET_REDIS_LIVE_QUERY_SMALL_TARGET_THRESHOLD Maximum number of targeted hosts for a live query to use the per-host reverse index instead of a fleet-wide bitfield, avoiding one GETBIT per query on every host check-in. Set to 0 to disable the reverse index and use the bitfield for all live queries. (default 1000)
vuln_processing.--redis_max_idle_conns: Env: FLEET_REDIS_MAX_IDLE_CONNS Redis maximum idle connections (default 3)
vuln_processing.--redis_max_open_conns: Env: FLEET_REDIS_MAX_OPEN_CONNS Redis maximum open connections, 0 means no limit
vuln_processing.--redis_password: Env: FLEET_REDIS_PASSWORD Redis server password (prefer env variable for security)
vuln_processing.--redis_read_timeout: Env: FLEET_REDIS_READ_TIMEOUT Redis maximum amount of time to wait for a read (receive) on a connection (default 10s)
vuln_processing.--redis_region: Env: FLEET_REDIS_REGION Redis server Elasticache region
vuln_processing.--redis_sts_assume_role_arn: Env: FLEET_REDIS_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--redis_sts_external_id: Env: FLEET_REDIS_STS_EXTERNAL_ID Optional unique identifier that can be used by the principal assuming the role to assert its identity
vuln_processing.--redis_tls_ca: Env: FLEET_REDIS_TLS_CA Redis TLS server CA
vuln_processing.--redis_tls_cert: Env: FLEET_REDIS_TLS_CERT Redis TLS client certificate path
vuln_processing.--redis_tls_handshake_timeout: Env: FLEET_REDIS_TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT Redis TLS handshake timeout (default 10s)
vuln_processing.--redis_tls_key: Env: FLEET_REDIS_TLS_KEY Redis TLS client key path
vuln_processing.--redis_tls_server_name: Env: FLEET_REDIS_TLS_SERVER_NAME Redis TLS server name
vuln_processing.--redis_use_tls: Env: FLEET_REDIS_USE_TLS Redis server enable TLS
vuln_processing.--redis_write_timeout: Env: FLEET_REDIS_WRITE_TIMEOUT Redis maximum amount of time to wait for a write (send) on a connection (default 10s)
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_access_key_id: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_ACCESS_KEY_ID Access Key ID for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_bucket: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_BUCKET Bucket where to store file carves
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_cleanup_concurrency: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_CLEANUP_CONCURRENCY Number of concurrent S3 HeadObject probes the carve cleanup performs (default 32)
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_cleanup_disabled: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_CLEANUP_DISABLED Disable the periodic cleanup that marks carves whose S3 object no longer exists as expired
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_cleanup_max_per_run: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_CLEANUP_MAX_PER_RUN Maximum number of carves the S3 cleanup reconciles (and S3 HeadObject requests it makes) per run (default 1000)
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_disable_ssl: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_DISABLE_SSL Disable SSL (typically for local testing)
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_endpoint_url: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_ENDPOINT_URL AWS Service Endpoint to use (leave blank for default service endpoints)
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_force_s3_path_style: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_FORCE_S3_PATH_STYLE Set this to true to force path-style addressing, i.e., http://s3.amazonaws.com/BUCKET/KEY
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_gcs_iam_auth: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_GCS_IAM_AUTH Use Google ADC bearer tokens for GCS endpoint authentication instead of S3 HMAC keys
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_prefix: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_PREFIX Prefix under which carves are stored
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_region: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_REGION AWS Region (if blank region is derived)
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_secret_access_key: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Secret Access Key for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_sts_assume_role_arn: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for AWS
vuln_processing.--s3_carves_sts_external_id: Env: FLEET_S3_CARVES_STS_EXTERNAL_ID Optional unique identifier that can be used by the principal assuming the role to assert its identity.
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_access_key_id: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_ACCESS_KEY_ID Access Key ID for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_bucket: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_BUCKET Bucket where to store uploaded software installers
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_cloudfront_url: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_CLOUDFRONT_URL CloudFront URL for software installers
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_cloudfront_url_: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_CLOUDFRONT_URL_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY CloudFront private key for URL signing
Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_CLOUDFRONT_URL_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY_ID CloudFront public key ID for URL signing
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_disable_ssl: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_DISABLE_SSL Disable SSL (typically for local testing)
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_endpoint_url: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_ENDPOINT_URL AWS Service Endpoint to use (leave blank for default service endpoints)
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_force_s3_path_s: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_FORCE_S3_PATH_STYLE Set this to true to force path-style addressing, i.e., http://s3.amazonaws.com/BUCKET/KEY
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_gcs_iam_auth: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_GCS_IAM_AUTH Use Google ADC bearer tokens for GCS endpoint authentication instead of S3 HMAC keys
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_prefix: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_PREFIX Prefix under which software installers are stored
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_region: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_REGION AWS Region (if blank region is derived)
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_secret_access_k: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Secret Access Key for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_signed_url: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_SIGNED_URL Hand out presigned GCS URLs for installer/in-house app/bootstrap downloads instead of proxying bytes (requires a storage.googleapis.com endpoint)
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_sts_assume_role: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for AWS
vuln_processing.--s3_software_installers_sts_external_id: Env: FLEET_S3_SOFTWARE_INSTALLERS_STS_EXTERNAL_ID Optional unique identifier that can be used by the principal assuming the role to assert its identity.
vuln_processing.--server_allow_private_network_integrati: Env: FLEET_SERVER_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_INTEGRATIONS Allow integration HTTP requests to private network addresses (RFC 1918). Loopback and cloud metadata addresses are always blocked regardless of this setting.
vuln_processing.--server_bypass_network_blocking: Env: FLEET_SERVER_BYPASS_NETWORK_BLOCKING Disable all outbound network blocking protections for integration HTTP requests (loopback, cloud metadata, and private network addresses). Only intended for environments where egress is already constrained by external infrastructure (e.g. an egress proxy or firewall) that Fleet's own checks would otherwise conflict with. This is an infrastructure-level setting and cannot be changed at runtime.
vuln_processing.--server_cert: Env: FLEET_SERVER_CERT Fleet TLS certificate path (default "./tools/osquery/fleet.crt")
vuln_processing.--server_cleanup_dist_targets_age: Env: FLEET_SERVER_CLEANUP_DIST_TARGETS_AGE Specifies the cleanup age for completed live query distributed targets. (default 24h0m0s)
vuln_processing.--server_default_max_request_body_size: Env: FLEET_SERVER_DEFAULT_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE Default maximum size in bytes for request bodies, certain endpoints will have higher limits (e.g. 10MiB, 500KB, 1G) (default "1MiB")
vuln_processing.--server_force_h2c: Env: FLEET_SERVER_FORCE_H2C Force the fleet server to use HTTP2 cleartext aka h2c (ignored if using TLS)
vuln_processing.--server_frequent_cleanups_enabled: Env: FLEET_SERVER_FREQUENT_CLEANUPS_ENABLED Enable frequent cleanups of expired data (15 minute interval)
vuln_processing.--server_gzip_responses: Env: FLEET_SERVER_GZIP_RESPONSES Enable gzip-compressed responses for supported clients
vuln_processing.--server_keepalive: Env: FLEET_SERVER_KEEPALIVE Controls whether HTTP keep-alives are enabled. (default true)
vuln_processing.--server_key: Env: FLEET_SERVER_KEY Fleet TLS key path (default "./tools/osquery/fleet.key")
vuln_processing.--server_max_installer_size: Env: FLEET_SERVER_MAX_INSTALLER_SIZE Maximum size in bytes for software installer uploads (e.g. 10GiB, 500MB, 1G) (default "10GiB")
vuln_processing.--server_private_key: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY Used for encrypting sensitive data, such as MDM certificates.
vuln_processing.--server_private_key_arn: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_ARN ARN of AWS Secrets Manager secret containing server private key
vuln_processing.--server_private_key_region: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_REGION AWS region of the Secrets Manager secret containing server private key
vuln_processing.--server_private_key_sts_assume_role_arn: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for accessing private key secret
vuln_processing.--server_private_key_sts_external_id: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_STS_EXTERNAL_ID External ID for STS role assumption when accessing private key secret
vuln_processing.--server_tls: Env: FLEET_SERVER_TLS Enable TLS (required for osqueryd communication) (default true)
vuln_processing.--server_tls_compatibility: Env: FLEET_SERVER_TLS_COMPATIBILITY TLS security profile choose one of modern or intermediate (default "intermediate")
vuln_processing.--server_trusted_proxies: Env: FLEET_SERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES Trusted proxy configuration for client IP extraction: 'none' (RemoteAddr only), a header name (e.g., 'True-Client-IP'), a hop count (e.g., '2'), or comma-separated IP/CIDR ranges
vuln_processing.--server_url_prefix: Env: FLEET_SERVER_URL_PREFIX URL prefix used on server and frontend endpoints
vuln_processing.--server_vpp_install_reap_timeout: Env: FLEET_SERVER_VPP_INSTALL_REAP_TIMEOUT Minimum time a stuck App Store or in-house app install must have been activated before Fleet fails it to release the host's activity queue. Zero or less turns the reaper off, and a value below server.vpp_verify_timeout is raised to it (default 24h0m0s)
vuln_processing.--server_vpp_verify_request_delay: Env: FLEET_SERVER_VPP_VERIFY_REQUEST_DELAY Delay in between requests to verify VPP app installs (default 5s)
vuln_processing.--server_vpp_verify_timeout: Env: FLEET_SERVER_VPP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT Maximum amount of time to wait for VPP app install verification (default 10m0s)
vuln_processing.--server_websockets_allow_unsafe_origin: Env: FLEET_SERVER_WEBSOCKETS_ALLOW_UNSAFE_ORIGIN Disable checking the origin header on websocket connections, this is sometimes necessary when proxies rewrite origin headers between the client and the Fleet webserver
vuln_processing.--ses_access_key_id: Env: FLEET_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID Access Key ID for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--ses_endpoint_url: Env: FLEET_SES_ENDPOINT_URL AWS Service Endpoint to use (leave empty for default service endpoints)
vuln_processing.--ses_region: Env: FLEET_SES_REGION AWS Region to use
vuln_processing.--ses_secret_access_key: Env: FLEET_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Secret Access Key for AWS authentication
vuln_processing.--ses_sender_domain: Env: FLEET_SES_SENDER_DOMAIN Optional domain to use in the From address for SES emails. If empty, Fleet uses the hostname from the Fleet Web Address (server_settings.server_url)
vuln_processing.--ses_source_arn: Env: FLEET_SES_SOURCE_ARN ARN of the identity that is associated with the sending authorization policy that permits you to send for the email address specified in the Source parameter
vuln_processing.--ses_sts_assume_role_arn: Env: FLEET_SES_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for AWS
vuln_processing.--ses_sts_external_id: Env: FLEET_SES_STS_EXTERNAL_ID Optional unique identifier that can be used by the principal assuming the role to assert its identity.
vuln_processing.--session_duration: Env: FLEET_SESSION_DURATION Duration session keys remain valid (i.e. 4h) (default 120h0m0s)
vuln_processing.--session_key_size: Env: FLEET_SESSION_KEY_SIZE Size of generated session keys (default 64)
vuln_processing.--splunk_index: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_INDEX Splunk index to send events to
vuln_processing.--splunk_insecure_skip_verify: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY Skip TLS certificate verification for Splunk HEC (for self-signed certs)
vuln_processing.--splunk_source: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_SOURCE Splunk source value for events
vuln_processing.--splunk_source_type: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_SOURCE_TYPE Splunk sourcetype value for events
vuln_processing.--splunk_token: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_TOKEN Splunk HEC authentication token
vuln_processing.--splunk_url: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_URL Splunk HEC URL (e.g. https://splunk.example.com:8088)
vuln_processing.--upgrades_allow_missing_migrations: Env: FLEET_UPGRADES_ALLOW_MISSING_MIGRATIONS Allow serve to run even if migrations are missing.
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_cisa_known_exploits_ur: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CISA_KNOWN_EXPLOITS_URL URL from which to get the latest CISA (Known exploited vulnerabilities) database. If empty, it will be downloaded from https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_cpe_database_url: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CPE_DATABASE_URL URL from which to get the latest CPE database. If empty, it will be downloaded from the latest release available at https://github.com/fleetdm/nvd/releases.
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_cpe_translations_url: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CPE_TRANSLATIONS_URL URL from which to get the latest CPE translations. If empty, it will be downloaded from the latest release available at https://github.com/fleetdm/nvd/releases.
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_current_instance_check: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CURRENT_INSTANCE_CHECKS Allows to manually select an instance to do the vulnerability processing. (default "auto")
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_cve_feed_prefix_url: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CVE_FEED_PREFIX_URL Prefix URL for the CVE data feed. If empty, default to https://nvd.nist.gov/
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_databases_path: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DATABASES_PATH Path where Fleet will download the data feeds to check CVEs (default "/tmp/vulndbs")
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_disable_data_sync: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_DATA_SYNC Skips synchronizing data streams and expects them to be available in the databases_path.
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_disable_schedule: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_SCHEDULE Set this to true when the vulnerability processing job is scheduled by an external mechanism
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_disable_win_os_vulnera: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_WIN_OS_VULNERABILITIES Don't sync installed Windows updates nor perform Windows OS vulnerability processing.
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_max_concurrency: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_MAX_CONCURRENCY Maximum number of concurrent database queries to use for processing vulnerabilities. (default 1)
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_osv_for_vulnerabilitie: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_OSV_FOR_VULNERABILITIES Use OSV (osv.dev) format for vulnerability detection instead of OVAL where supported. (default true)
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_periodicity: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_PERIODICITY How much time to wait between processing software for vulnerabilities. (default 1h0m0s)
vuln_processing.--vulnerabilities_recent_vulnerability_m: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_RECENT_VULNERABILITY_MAX_AGE Maximum age of the published date of a vulnerability (CVE) to be considered 'recent'. (default 720h0m0s)
vuln_processing.--webhook_result_url: Env: FLEET_WEBHOOK_RESULT_URL Webhook URL for osquery result logs
vuln_processing.--webhook_status_url: Env: FLEET_WEBHOOK_STATUS_URL Webhook URL for osquery status logs

help.text:
Fleet server (https://fleetdm.com)

Configurable Options:

Options may be supplied in a yaml configuration file or via environment
variables. You only need to define the configuration values for which you
wish to override the default value.

Usage:
  fleet [command]

Available Commands:
  completion      Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  config_dump     Dump the parsed configuration in yaml format
  help            Help about any command
  prepare         Subcommands for initializing Fleet infrastructure
  serve           Launch the Fleet server
  version         Print Fleet version
  vuln_processing Run the vulnerability processing features of Fleet

Flags:

      --activity_enable_audit_log                                                       Env: FLEET_ACTIVITY_ENABLE_AUDIT_LOG
                                                                                        		Enable audit logs

                                                                                        		Enable compression for the rotated osquery log files
      --filesystem_enable_log_rotation                                                  Env: FLEET_FILESYSTEM_ENABLE_LOG_ROTATION
                                                                                        		Enable automatic rotation for osquery log files
      --filesystem_max_age int                                                          Env: FLEET_FILESYSTEM_MAX_AGE
                                                                                        		Maximum number of days to retain old log files based on the timestamp encoded in their filename. Setting to zero wil retain old log files indefinitely (only valid if enable_log_rotation is true) default is 28 days (default 28)

                                                                                        		Maximum number of old log files to retain. Setting to zero will retain all old log files (only valid if enable_log_rotation is true) default is 3 (default 3)
      --filesystem_max_size int                                                         Env: FLEET_FILESYSTEM_MAX_SIZE

      --filesystem_result_log_file string                                               Env: FLEET_FILESYSTEM_RESULT_LOG_FILE
                                                                                        		Log file path to use for result logs (default "/tmp/osquery_result")
      --filesystem_status_log_file string                                               Env: FLEET_FILESYSTEM_STATUS_LOG_FILE

--H.help: Add a HTTP request header in key:value format

--activity-dsn.help: MySQL DSN for the activity seeder (default fleet:insecure@tcp(localhost:3306)/fleet)

--activity-host-id.help: host_id used by the activity seeder for host-scoped rows (default 1)

--activity_audit_log_plugin.help: Env: FLEET_ACTIVITY_AUDIT_LOG_PLUGIN Log plugin to use for audit logs (default "filesystem")

--actor-id.help: user_id stamped on inserted rows (must exist in users)

--all.help: Test every CIS policy in the policy file.

--allow-unknown-keys.help: Log unknown keys as warnings instead of failing with errors

--allowrenew.help: do not allow renewal until n days before expiry, set to 0 to always allow

--android_app_count.help: Number of installed apps each Android device reports

--android_non_compliance_prob.help: Probability of an Android STATUS_REPORT including non-compliance details [0, 1]

--android_proxy_address.help: Address of the mock AMAPI proxy (e.g., http://localhost:9999)

--android_pubsub_token.help: PubSub token for authenticating fake Android device messages to Fleet

--android_status_interval.help: Interval between Android STATUS_REPORT messages (real devices report ~every 24h; lower values stress test Fleet harder)

--api_token.help: API authentication token to use on API calls

--app-store-connect-api-key-content.help: Contents of the .p8 App Store Connect API key

--app-store-connect-api-key-id.help: App Store Connect API key used for notarization

--app-store-connect-api-key-issuer.help: Issuer of the App Store Connect API key

--app_enable_scheduled_query_stats.help: Env: FLEET_APP_ENABLE_SCHEDULED_QUERY_STATS If true (default) it gets scheduled query stats from hosts (default true)

--app_invite_token_validity_period.help: Env: FLEET_APP_INVITE_TOKEN_VALIDITY_PERIOD Duration invite tokens remain valid (i.e. 1h) (default 120h0m0s)

--app_token_key.help: Env: FLEET_APP_TOKEN_KEY Secret key for generating invite and reset tokens (default "CHANGEME")

--app_token_key_size.help: Env: FLEET_APP_TOKEN_KEY_SIZE Size of generated tokens (default 24)

--apply.help: Execute SQL against the database in a transaction

--auth-proxy-url.help: Reverse proxy URL target for MDM-authenticated HTTP requests

--batches.help: Number of full passes to insert (each pass writes one row per template with a fresh run tag)

--no-prompt.help: disable prompting before migrations (for use in scripts)

--node_key_file.help: File with node keys to use

--older-than.help: Only pull issues with an ID less than this (for e.g. continuing after being rate-limited)

--one-time-challenge.help: consume each generated challenge after a single successful PKIOperation (ignored when -challenge is set)

--only-manual.help: Only run tests that require manual user interaction (MANUAL). Skip all automated tests. Useful for walking through the checks that can't be scripted.

--only-mdm.help: Only run MDM-dependent tests (PROFILE and ORG_DECISION). Skip script-based and manual tests. Useful when validating MDM profile delivery.

--only-scripts.help: Only run script-based tests (PASS_FAIL and PASS_ONLY). Skip MDM profile tests, org-decision tests, and manual prompts. Useful for running a fast, fully-automated subset.

--only_already_enrolled.help: Only start agents that are already enrolled

--orbit-channel.help: Update channel of Orbit to use

--orbit_prob.help: Probability of a host being identified as orbit install [0, 1]

--osquery-db.help: Sets a custom osquery database directory, it must be an absolute path (requires orbit >= v1.22.0)

--osquery-flagfile.help: Flagfile to package and provide to osquery

--osquery_allow_body_auth_fallback.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ALLOW_BODY_AUTH_FALLBACK Selects how host-authenticated osquery requests are authenticated. When true (default), only body-based node_key is used for authentication. When false, the nodey_key header is required for authentication and the body's node_key is ignored; pre-auth rejects absent/invalid headers before the body is read. (default true)

--osquery_async_host_collect_interval.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_COLLECT_INTERVAL Interval to collect asynchronous host-reported query results (e.g. '30s' or set per task 'label_membership=10s&policy_membership=1m') (default "30s")

--osquery_async_host_collect_lock_timeou.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_COLLECT_LOCK_TIMEOUT Timeout of the exclusive lock held during async host collection (e.g., '30s' or set per task 'label_membership=10s&policy_membership=1m' (default "1m0s")

--osquery_async_host_collect_log_stats_i.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_COLLECT_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL Interval at which async host collection statistics are logged (0 disables logging of stats) (default 1m0s)

--osquery_async_host_collect_max_jitter_.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_COLLECT_MAX_JITTER_PERCENT Maximum percentage of the interval to collect asynchronous host results (default 10)

--osquery_async_host_delete_batch.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_DELETE_BATCH Batch size for async collection deletes in mysql (default 2000)

--osquery_async_host_insert_batch.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_INSERT_BATCH Batch size for async collection inserts in mysql (default 2000)

--osquery_async_host_redis_pop_count.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_REDIS_POP_COUNT Batch size to pop items from redis in async collection (default 1000)

--osquery_async_host_update_batch.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ASYNC_HOST_UPDATE_BATCH Batch size for async collection updates in mysql (default 1000)

--osquery_detail_update_interval.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_DETAIL_UPDATE_INTERVAL Interval to update host details (i.e. 1h) (default 1h0m0s)

--osquery_enable_async_host_processing.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ENABLE_ASYNC_HOST_PROCESSING Enable asynchronous processing of host-reported query results (either 'true'/'false' or set per task, e.g., 'label_membership=true&policy_membership=true') (default "false")

--osquery_enable_log_rotation.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ENABLE_LOG_ROTATION (DEPRECATED: Use filesystem.enable_log_rotation) Enable automatic rotation for osquery log files

--osquery_enroll_cooldown.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_ENROLL_COOLDOWN Cooldown period for duplicate host enrollment (default off)

--osquery_host_identifier.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_HOST_IDENTIFIER Identifier used to uniquely determine osquery clients (default "provided")

--osquery_label_update_interval.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_LABEL_UPDATE_INTERVAL Interval to update host label membership (i.e. 1h) (default 1h0m0s)

--osquery_max_distributed_write_body_siz.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_MAX_DISTRIBUTED_WRITE_BODY_SIZE Maximum body size for the osquery/distributed/write endpoint (e.g. 10MiB, 500KB). 0 means use the built-in default (5MiB). Only applied when osquery.allow_body_auth_fallback is true. In header-auth mode (false) the route is not subject to any body size limit; this value is ignored. (default "0")

--osquery_max_jitter_percent.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_MAX_JITTER_PERCENT Maximum percentage of the interval to add as jitter (default 10)

--osquery_max_log_write_body_size.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_MAX_LOG_WRITE_BODY_SIZE Maximum body size for the osquery/log endpoint (e.g. 10MiB, 500KB). 0 means use the built-in default (10MiB). Only applied when osquery.allow_body_auth_fallback is true. In header-auth mode (false) the route is not subject to any body size limit; this value is ignored. (default "0")

--osquery_min_software_last_opened_at_di.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_MIN_SOFTWARE_LAST_OPENED_AT_DIFF Minimum time difference of the software's last opened timestamp (compared to the last one saved) to trigger an update to the database (default 2m0s)

--osquery_policy_update_interval.help: Env: FLEET_OSQUERY_POLICY_UPDATE_INTERVAL Interval to update host policy membership (i.e. 1h) (default 1h0m0s)

--password.help: Password to use to log in (recommended to use interactive entry)

--serial-number.help: serial number of a device to get the device details

--server-private-key.help: fleet server's private key (to decrypt MDM assets)

--server_allow_private_network_integrati.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_INTEGRATIONS Allow integration HTTP requests to private network addresses (RFC 1918). Loopback and cloud metadata addresses are always blocked regardless of this setting.

--server_bypass_network_blocking.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_BYPASS_NETWORK_BLOCKING Disable all outbound network blocking protections for integration HTTP requests (loopback, cloud metadata, and private network addresses). Only intended for environments where egress is already constrained by external infrastructure (e.g. an egress proxy or firewall) that Fleet's own checks would otherwise conflict with. This is an infrastructure-level setting and cannot be changed at runtime.

--server_cert.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_CERT Fleet TLS certificate path (default "./tools/osquery/fleet.crt")

--server_cleanup_dist_targets_age.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_CLEANUP_DIST_TARGETS_AGE Specifies the cleanup age for completed live query distributed targets. (default 24h0m0s)

--server_default_max_request_body_size.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_DEFAULT_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE Default maximum size in bytes for request bodies, certain endpoints will have higher limits (e.g. 10MiB, 500KB, 1G) (default "1MiB")

--server_force_h2c.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_FORCE_H2C Force the fleet server to use HTTP2 cleartext aka h2c (ignored if using TLS)

--server_frequent_cleanups_enabled.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_FREQUENT_CLEANUPS_ENABLED Enable frequent cleanups of expired data (15 minute interval)

--server_gzip_responses.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_GZIP_RESPONSES Enable gzip-compressed responses for supported clients

--server_keepalive.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_KEEPALIVE Controls whether HTTP keep-alives are enabled. (default true)

--server_key.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_KEY Fleet TLS key path (default "./tools/osquery/fleet.key")

--server_max_installer_size.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_MAX_INSTALLER_SIZE Maximum size in bytes for software installer uploads (e.g. 10GiB, 500MB, 1G) (default "10GiB")

--server_private_key.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY Used for encrypting sensitive data, such as MDM certificates.

--server_private_key_arn.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_ARN ARN of AWS Secrets Manager secret containing server private key

--server_private_key_region.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_REGION AWS region of the Secrets Manager secret containing server private key

--server_private_key_sts_assume_role_arn.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for accessing private key secret

--server_private_key_sts_external_id.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY_STS_EXTERNAL_ID External ID for STS role assumption when accessing private key secret

--server_tls.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_TLS Enable TLS (required for osqueryd communication) (default true)

--server_tls_compatibility.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_TLS_COMPATIBILITY TLS security profile choose one of modern or intermediate (default "intermediate")

--server_trusted_proxies.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES Trusted proxy configuration for client IP extraction: 'none' (RemoteAddr only), a header name (e.g., 'True-Client-IP'), a hop count (e.g., '2'), or comma-separated IP/CIDR ranges

--server_url.help: URL (with protocol and port of osquery server)

--server_url_prefix.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_URL_PREFIX URL prefix used on server and frontend endpoints

--server_vpp_install_reap_timeout.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_VPP_INSTALL_REAP_TIMEOUT Minimum time a stuck App Store or in-house app install must have been activated before Fleet fails it to release the host's activity queue. Zero or less turns the reaper off, and a value below server.vpp_verify_timeout is raised to it (default 24h0m0s)

--server_vpp_verify_request_delay.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_VPP_VERIFY_REQUEST_DELAY Delay in between requests to verify VPP app installs (default 5s)

--server_vpp_verify_timeout.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_VPP_VERIFY_TIMEOUT Maximum amount of time to wait for VPP app install verification (default 10m0s)

--server_websockets_allow_unsafe_origin.help: Env: FLEET_SERVER_WEBSOCKETS_ALLOW_UNSAFE_ORIGIN Disable checking the origin header on websocket connections, this is sometimes necessary when proxies rewrite origin headers between the client and the Fleet webserver

--service.help: Install orbit/osquery with a persistence service (launchd, systemd, etc.)

--ses_access_key_id.help: Env: FLEET_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID Access Key ID for AWS authentication

--ses_endpoint_url.help: Env: FLEET_SES_ENDPOINT_URL AWS Service Endpoint to use (leave empty for default service endpoints)

--ses_region.help: Env: FLEET_SES_REGION AWS Region to use

--ses_secret_access_key.help: Env: FLEET_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Secret Access Key for AWS authentication

--ses_sender_domain.help: Env: FLEET_SES_SENDER_DOMAIN Optional domain to use in the From address for SES emails. If empty, Fleet uses the hostname from the Fleet Web Address (server_settings.server_url)

--ses_source_arn.help: Env: FLEET_SES_SOURCE_ARN ARN of the identity that is associated with the sending authorization policy that permits you to send for the email address specified in the Source parameter

--ses_sts_assume_role_arn.help: Env: FLEET_SES_STS_ASSUME_ROLE_ARN ARN of role to assume for AWS

--ses_sts_external_id.help: Env: FLEET_SES_STS_EXTERNAL_ID Optional unique identifier that can be used by the principal assuming the role to assert its identity.

--session_duration.help: Env: FLEET_SESSION_DURATION Duration session keys remain valid (i.e. 4h) (default 120h0m0s)

--session_key_size.help: Env: FLEET_SESSION_KEY_SIZE Size of generated session keys (default 64)

--sign-identity.help: Identity to use for macOS codesigning

--sign-server-attrs.help: sign cert attrs for server usage

--skip-no-script.help: Skip MANUAL-type tests (policies with no automation) instead of prompting the user to perform the steps. MDM profile tests and org-decision tests still run. (--skip-no-script is kept as a deprecated alias.)

--socket.help: Path to the extensions UNIX domain socket

--software_db_path.help: Path to software.db (SQLite database with realistic software data). Auto-generates from software.sql if missing.

--software_installer_install_fail_prob.help: Probability of the install script failing

--software_installer_post_install_fail_p.help: Probability of the post-install script failing

--software_installer_pre_install_fail_pr.help: Probability of the pre-install query failing

--software_query_fail_prob.help: Probability of the software query failing

--software_renaming.help: Enable software renaming for duplicate bundle identifiers

--software_vscode_extensions_query_fail_.help: Probability of the software vscode_extensions query failing

--source-migration.help: Name of the source migration file to bump (required).

--splunk_index.help: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_INDEX Splunk index to send events to

--splunk_insecure_skip_verify.help: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY Skip TLS certificate verification for Splunk HEC (for self-signed certs)

--splunk_source.help: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_SOURCE Splunk source value for events

--splunk_source_type.help: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_SOURCE_TYPE Splunk sourcetype value for events

--splunk_token.help: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_TOKEN Splunk HEC authentication token

--splunk_url.help: Env: FLEET_SPLUNK_URL Splunk HEC URL (e.g. https://splunk.example.com:8088)

--start-date.help: start date (YYYY-MM-DD), defaults to now - days

--start_period.help: Duration to spread start of hosts over

--strip-emojis.help: Strip emojis from project titles and statuses

--tag.help: Tags to apply to the target (multiple may be specified)

--tart-image.help: Override the tart base image. By default, the image is chosen based on --macos-version: 13=ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-ventura-base:latest, 14=ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-sonoma-base:latest, 15=ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-sequoia-base:latest, 26=ghcr.io/cirruslabs/macos-tahoe-base:latest.

--team.help: **Available in Fleet Premium.** Only output the configuration files of the fleet with the specified name. Global or "Unassigned" configuration may be output using `--team global` or `--team no-team`.

--team-id.help: Team to enroll into. -1 (default) = interactive pick. 0 = no team / global.

--team-name.help: Team to enroll into, by name. Overrides --team-id.

--team_count.help: Number of teams to create for the load test

--tf-dir.help: Path to the db-temp Terraform root (default: %(default)s)

--theme.help: Easter-egg theme: mix, hitchhikers, goodplace, parksrec, tng, lotr, dbz, robin_williams, ghibli, cosmere, sailor_moon

--timeout.help: How long to run query before exiting (10s, 1h, etc.)

--tls.help: serve HTTPS instead of HTTP (real NDES is HTTPS)

--tls-mode.help: TLS verification mode: skip-verify, verify-ca, verify-identity

--total_host_count.help: Total number of hosts across all containers (if 0, uses host_count)

--ua-zl-dc.help: reply with zero-length DigestChallenge for UserAuthenticate

--ubuntu.help: Number of Ubuntu software rows to insert

--unenroll.help: Unenroll from MDM instead of enrolling

--unique_software_count.help: Number of unique software installed on each host

--unique_software_uninstall_count.help: Number of unique software to uninstall

--unique_software_uninstall_prob.help: Probability of uninstalling unique_software_uninstall_count common software/s

--unique_user_count.help: Number of unique host users reported to fleet

--unique_vscode_extensions_software_coun.help: Number of unique vscode_extensions software installed on each host

--unique_vscode_extensions_software_unin.help: Number of unique vscode_extensions software to uninstall

--update.help: Update the generated files with the current cacheable items

--update-interval.help: Interval that Orbit will use to check for new updates (10s, 1h, etc.)

--update-roots.help: Root key JSON metadata for update server (from fleetctl updates roots)

--update-tls-certificate.help: Path to the update server TLS certificate chain

--update-tls-client-certificate.help: Path to a TLS client certificate to use when connecting to the update server. This functionality is licensed under the Fleet EE License. Usage requires a current Fleet EE subscription.

--update-tls-client-key.help: Path to a TLS client private key to use when connecting to the update server. This functionality is licensed under the Fleet EE License. Usage requires a current Fleet EE subscription.

--upgrades_allow_missing_migrations.help: Env: FLEET_UPGRADES_ALLOW_MISSING_MIGRATIONS Allow serve to run even if migrations are missing.

--url-prefix.help: Specify URL Prefix to use with Fleet server (copy from server configuration)

--use-system-configuration.help: Try to read --fleet-url and --enroll-secret using configuration in the host (currently only macOS profiles are supported)

--use-tracked-cves.help: for --dataset cve, auto-discover entity IDs from the production tracked-CVE query (overrides --entity-ids)

--user-count.help: How many seeded users to give an IDP account

--validate.help: Validate the certificate, including client authentication to the Apple sandbox

--validity-days.help: validity period in days for issued certificates

--verbose.help: Log detailed information when building the package

--vm-name.help: Name for the tart VM. If a VM with this name already exists, it will be deleted and recreated. (default: cis-test-macos-{version})

--vulnerabilities_cisa_known_exploits_ur.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CISA_KNOWN_EXPLOITS_URL URL from which to get the latest CISA (Known exploited vulnerabilities) database. If empty, it will be downloaded from https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json

--vulnerabilities_cpe_database_url.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CPE_DATABASE_URL URL from which to get the latest CPE database. If empty, it will be downloaded from the latest release available at https://github.com/fleetdm/nvd/releases.

--vulnerabilities_cpe_translations_url.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CPE_TRANSLATIONS_URL URL from which to get the latest CPE translations. If empty, it will be downloaded from the latest release available at https://github.com/fleetdm/nvd/releases.

--vulnerabilities_current_instance_check.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CURRENT_INSTANCE_CHECKS Allows to manually select an instance to do the vulnerability processing. (default "auto")

--vulnerabilities_cve_feed_prefix_url.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_CVE_FEED_PREFIX_URL Prefix URL for the CVE data feed. If empty, default to https://nvd.nist.gov/

--vulnerabilities_databases_path.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DATABASES_PATH Path where Fleet will download the data feeds to check CVEs (default "/tmp/vulndbs")

--vulnerabilities_disable_data_sync.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_DATA_SYNC Skips synchronizing data streams and expects them to be available in the databases_path.

--vulnerabilities_disable_schedule.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_SCHEDULE Set this to true when the vulnerability processing job is scheduled by an external mechanism

--vulnerabilities_disable_win_os_vulnera.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_DISABLE_WIN_OS_VULNERABILITIES Don't sync installed Windows updates nor perform Windows OS vulnerability processing.

--vulnerabilities_max_concurrency.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_MAX_CONCURRENCY Maximum number of concurrent database queries to use for processing vulnerabilities. (default 1)

--vulnerabilities_osv_for_vulnerabilitie.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_OSV_FOR_VULNERABILITIES Use OSV (osv.dev) format for vulnerability detection instead of OVAL where supported. (default true)

--vulnerabilities_periodicity.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_PERIODICITY How much time to wait between processing software for vulnerabilities. (default 1h0m0s)

--vulnerabilities_recent_vulnerability_m.help: Env: FLEET_VULNERABILITIES_RECENT_VULNERABILITY_MAX_AGE Maximum age of the published date of a vulnerability (CVE) to be considered 'recent'. (default 720h0m0s)

--vulnerable_software_count.help: Number of vulnerable installed applications reported to fleet.  Use -1 to load all vulnerable software.

--webhook_result_url.help: Env: FLEET_WEBHOOK_RESULT_URL Webhook URL for osquery result logs

--webhook_status_url.help: Env: FLEET_WEBHOOK_STATUS_URL Webhook URL for osquery status logs

--windows.help: Number of Windows software rows to insert

--with-table-stats.help: Show approximate table row counts after migrations

--with_last_opened_software_count.help: Number of applications that may report a last opened timestamp to fleet

--without-milestone.help: Bug milestones to exclude (to simulate a release going GA)

-a.help: Path to the `.app` bundle (e.g. `/Applications/Safari.app`). Required if `-i` is not provided.

-allowrenew.help: do not allow renewal until n days before expiry, set to 0 to always allow (default "14")

-auth-token.help: Auth token for remote flag updates (remote updates disabled if not provided)

-ca-fingerprint.help: SHA-256 digest of CA certificate for NDES server. Note: Changed from MD5.

-certificate.help: certificate path, if there is no key, scepclient will create one

-crtvalid.help: validity for new client certificates in days (default "365")

-csrverifierexec.help: will be passed the CSRs for verification

-f.help: flags - Additional flags to apply to `fleetctl package`.

-i.help: Path to a PNG icon file. Required if `-a` is not provided. The icon will be resized to 128x128 if larger.

-migrate-percentage.help: Percentage of clients to migrate from existing MDM to Fleet

-migrate-udids.help: Space/newline-delimited list of UDIDs to migrate always

-o.help: output - Default: Current location - Directory in which to place the generated packages.

-p.help: packages - Default: "all" - The types of installer packages to create for each team.

-private-key.help: private key path, if there is no key, scepclient will create one

-s.help: Slug name for the Fleet-maintained app (required). The portion before the slash will be used in the output filenames.

-server-address.help: Address for server to listen on (default ":8080")

-u.help: The url of the Fleet server.

-x.help: dry_run - Test prossesing the file, creating the team in Fleet, and generating packages without applying any changes to the server.

activities.help: Seed fake activities directly into MySQL (non-idempotent)

all.help: Seed one row of every activity type (~161 rows per batch)

average-open-days.help: Calculate the average number of days bugs are open

cas.help: Seed fake certificate authorities directly into MySQL (non-idempotent)

config_dump.help: Dump the parsed configuration in yaml format

db.help: Given correct database configurations, prepare the databases for use

dibble.help: Fleet's seed slinger — plant test data into a Fleet server

enroll-secrets.help: Seed per-team enroll secrets (the credential fleetd uses to join a team)

estimated.help: Get estimated GitHub issues from the drafting project filtered by project label

forecast.help: Calculate effort forecast for a milestone based on t-shirt sizes

hosts.help: Pick a team and run osquery-perf against it (single-select radio + inline run)

identifier.help: Identifier of profile to remove (ex. com.example.profile)

idp.help: Create IDP accounts for seeded users and assign them to hosts (direct MySQL)

issues-with-historical-label.help: Find issues created since a date that had a specific label at any point

migration-cleanup.help: Detect and fix Fleet migration renumbering

mobileconfig.help: Path to mobileconfig file (profile) to install

pin.help: The six-character PIN for Find My.

ping.help: Verify dibble can reach the Fleet API

policies.help: Seed global policies (and a couple per existing team)

project.help: Get GitHub issues from a project

query.help: optional DeviceInformation queries (ex. Model, OSVersion, etc.)

report.help: Print a table of issues and their project statuses for a milestone

sprint.help: Get GitHub issues in the current sprint for a project (use -p for previous sprint)

sync-estimates.help: Sync estimates for issues on the Releases planning project from issues or sub-issues.

users.help: Seed Fleet users with themed names and rotating roles

view.help: Interactive view of issues in a milestone

vuln_processing.help: Run the vulnerability processing features of Fleet

vulns.help: Seed software rows directly into MySQL for the vuln scanner to chew on
